newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers seeking winter cover.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers seeking winter cover.

text.p: European spinning mills bought some upland cotton for shipment during the 1996/97 winter amid steady prices, the Bremen Cotton Exchange's fortnightly report said on Monday.
Nearby supplies of medium and low grades were tight.
The report also mentioned activity in long and extra long staples, especially Egyptian grades, but also U.S. and Israel Pima.
Bremen cotton stocks Bremen were reduced by 1,704 bales in the fortnight ended Oct 4 to 57,057 bales, compared with 58,275 bales recorded a year earlier.
The exchange listed fourth quarter 1996 offers of Zimbabwe and Greek cottons as well as Central Asian grades for the first half of 1997 and Westafricans, including Chad, for Jan-Dec 1997.
